proposals.before: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinxiang.
proposals.after: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinchang.

proposals.before: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinxiang.
proposals.after: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinchang.
proposals.reason: 新昌鄉侯 is Xinchang, not Xinxiang. The idiomatic and literal English both transliterate the fief wrong.

proposals.before: He Zeng and his colleagues firmly argued, "The Central Pacification Army is intelligent, divinely martial, and has talent beyond the age.
proposals.after: He Zeng and his colleagues firmly argued, "The central commander of the army is intelligent, divinely martial, and has talent beyond the age.
proposals.reason: 中撫軍 is Sima Yan's office (central commander of the army), not an army called the Central Pacification Army. The literal English already says central commander.

proposals.before: That month a man of extraordinary height appeared at Xiangwu, three zhang tall, and announced to the people of the district, Wang Shi, "Now there shall be great peace."
proposals.after: That month a man of extraordinary height appeared at Xiangwu, three zhang tall, and told the county man Wang Shi, "Now there shall be great peace."
proposals.reason: 縣人王始 is one man, the county man Wang Shi, not 'the people of the district' plus an appositive. The idiomatic English already says 'the county man Wang Shi'.

proposals.before: On yiwei he ordered the middle (district) heads of commanderies to recommend the long-neglected and obstructed according to six criteria: first, loyalty and conscientiousness sacrificing self; second, filial respect fulfilling ritual; third, harmony among brothers; fourth, purity of person with humble industry; fifth, trustworthiness and righteousness that can be relied upon; sixth, learning for one’s own moral cultivation.
proposals.after: On yiwei he ordered the impartial evaluators (zhongzheng) of commanderies to recommend the long-neglected and obstructed according to six criteria: first, loyalty and conscientiousness sacrificing self; second, filial respect fulfilling ritual; third, harmony among brothers; fourth, purity of person with humble industry; fifth, trustworthiness and righteousness that can be relied upon; sixth, learning for one’s own moral cultivation.
proposals.reason: 郡中正 is the commandery zhongzheng (evaluator), not a 'middle head'. The idiomatic English already says commandery-level evaluators.

proposals.before: On the day bingyin, winter, twelfth month, first year of Taishi, he set up an altar south of the suburbs; the hundred officials stood in place, together with the southern chanyu of the Xiongnu and visitors from the four barbarians numbering in the tens of thousands; he kindled the firewood offering and reported the category of his accession to the high lord, saying, "The emperor, your subject Yan, dares to use a black bull clearly to announce to august heaven and august earth: the Wei emperor has examined and aligned with the royal fortune and, clarifying heaven’s bright mandate, has used it to command Yan.

proposals.before: A sweep of enfeoffments followed: granduncle Fu as king of Anping, a ring of royal uncles and cousins as kings of Pingyuan, Fufeng, Dongguan, Ru'yin, Liang, Langye, and more, his brother You as king of Qi, and dozens of kinsmen given kingdoms from Bohai to Dongping (footnotes [1][2] preserved in the text).

proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops most of the named kings and flattens 叔父, 從伯父, 從叔父, 從父兄, and 從父弟 into one 'ring of uncles and cousins'.

proposals.before: He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping, his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ru'yin, Tong as king of Liang, Lun as king of Langye, his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Le'an, Ji as king of Yan, [1] his cousin once removed Wang as king of Yiyang, his uncles Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, Bin as king of Chen, his cousin Hong as king of Hejian, and his cousin Mao as king of Dongping.
proposals.after: He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping, his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ru'yin, Tong as king of Liang, Lun as king of Langye, his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Le'an, Ji as king of Yan, [1] his cousin once removed Wang as king of Yiyang, his father's younger cousins Fu (輔) as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui (瑰) as king of Taiyuan, Gui (珪) as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui (綏) as king of Fanyang, Sui (遂) as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, and Bin as king of Chen, his cousin Hong as king of Hejian, and his cousin Mao as king of Dongping.
proposals.reason: 皇從叔父 is a father's younger cousin, not an uncle, and the repeated Gui and Sui hide 瑰/珪 and 綏/遂.

proposals.after: He appointed Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry, grand marshal and duke of Leling; Chen Qian duke of Gaoping; Jia Chong general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Lu; Pei Xiu duke of Julu; Xun Xu duke of Jibei; Zheng Chong grand tutor and duke of Shouguang; Wang Xiang grand guardian and duke of Suiling; He Zeng grand commandant and duke of Langling; Wang Chen general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling; Xun Yi duke of Linhuai; and Wei Guan duke of Ziyang.

proposals.before: Summer, fifth month, wuchen: “The Chenliu king, Cao Shang, still files humble memorials on trifles—that is no way to honor him.
proposals.after: Summer, fifth month, wuchen: “The Chenliu king still conducts himself with modesty and files a memorial on every trifle—that is no way to honor him.
proposals.reason: 操尚謙沖 means his conduct is still modest. Cao Shang is not a name; the Wei king of Chenliu is Cao Huan, already on the throne-abdication record.

proposals.before: In summer, fifth month, on wuchen the edict said, "The king of Chenliu, Cao Shang, is still modest; on every matter he submits a memorial—this is not the way to show him special honor.
proposals.after: In summer, fifth month, on wuchen the edict said, "The king of Chenliu still conducts himself with modesty and submits a memorial on every matter—this is not the way to show him special honor.

proposals.after: On renzi [5] Wang Chen—swift-cavalry general and duke of Boling—passed away.

proposals.after: On wuzi he mused: “When the ancients set up symbolic punishments, the multitude did not offend; today we slaughter whole clans yet treason persists—what has become of moral government?
proposals.reason: 古設象刑 names no Yao or Shun. The idiomatic English inserts them. The literal English does not.

proposals.before: Second month, gengzi: the Chenliu ex-emperor’s apanage gained a full household staff—chancellor, household director, tomb wardens, artisans, cooks, and a band with carriages.
proposals.after: Second month, gengzi: the Shanyang duke’s state gained a full household staff—chancellor, household director, tomb wardens, artisans, cooks, and a band with carriages.
proposals.reason: 山陽公國 is the duke of Shanyang, not the king of Chenliu. The literal English already says mountain-yang duke.

proposals.before: December: Yang Zhao failed against Lu Kang and pulled back.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month: Yang Zhao failed against Lu Kang and pulled back.

proposals.before: May was rainless.

proposals.after: The second month saw Ping province carved from five Youzhou counties.
proposals.reason: 二月 is the lunar second month, not February.

proposals.after: In summer, the fourth month, on jiwei: Xun Yi, grand commandant and duke of Linhuai, died.

proposals.after: Eighth month: Liang tribes raided Jincheng until Sima Jun, king of Ru'yin, cut down chiefs such as Qi Wenni.

proposals.after: Wu generals Sun Zun and Li Cheng led a host to raid Jiangxia; prefect Ji Xi defeated them.

proposals.before: December: a comet trailed through Zhen.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month: a comet trailed through Zhen.
proposals.reason: 十二月 is the lunar twelfth month, not December.

proposals.before: Engineers cut a channel through southern Shanxi to swing the river east into the Luo and ease grain barges.
proposals.after: Engineers cut a channel through the southern Shan range to swing the river east into the Luo and ease grain barges.
proposals.reason: 陝南 is the range south of Shan (Shaan), not Shanxi province. The literal already says Shaan.

proposals.before: February brought relief for families swamped with daughters: any household raising five girls was excused from labor levies, so married soldiers could still serve without ruining their kin.
proposals.after: The second month brought relief for families swamped with daughters: any household raising five girls was excused from labor levies, so married soldiers could still serve without ruining their kin.

proposals.after: Earlier, Dunhuang had fallen into chaos after Yin Qu’s death: Linghu Feng ousted Liang Cheng, the magistrate who was acting as prefect and seized the prefecture.
proposals.reason: 梁澄 was magistrate of Dunhuang (敦煌令) and was ordered to act as prefect. The idiomatic English calls him an acting magistrate.

proposals.before: Jiaxu [15]: a comet shone in Di.
proposals.after: Jiaxu [15]: a comet shone in the asterism Di.
proposals.reason: 氐 here is the lunar lodge, which the literal already calls an asterism. It is not the Di people.

proposals.before: November: twin white dragons in Liang.
proposals.after: In the eleventh month: twin white dragons in Liang.
proposals.reason: 十一月 is the lunar eleventh month, not November.

proposals.before: Zheng Chong, Xun Yi, Shi Bao, Pei Xiu, Wang Shen, Prince Fu of Anping, He Zeng, Jia Chong, Chen Qian, Xun Xu, Yang Hu, Prince You of Qi, and others were all entered among those honored in commemorative offerings.

proposals.after: In the twelfth month he called scholar Huangfu Mi to tutor the heir and made empress Yang’s father Yang Jun marquis of Linjin.

proposals.after: In the sixth month: flash floods in Yi and Liang drowned three hundred and swamped auxiliary granaries.
proposals.reason: 六月 is the lunar sixth month, not June.

proposals.after: Guihai: a wholesale rotation of princely fiefs—Liang to Runan, Zhou to Langye, Jun to Fufeng, Lun to Zhao, Fu (輔) of Bohai to Taiyuan, Yong (顒) of Taiyuan to Hejian, Ling (陵) of Beihai to Rencheng, Bin (斌) of Chen to Xihe, Jian (柬) of Runan to Nanyang, Dan (耽) of Jinan to Zhongshan, and Wei (威) of Hejian to Zhangwu.

proposals.before: December: Sun Shen raided Jiangxia and Runan, dragging off a thousand families.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month: Sun Shen raided Jiangxia and Runan, dragging off a thousand families.
proposals.reason: 十二月 is the lunar twelfth month, not December.

proposals.after: Liang inspector Yang Xin died in defeat at Wuwei fighting Ruluobaneng and others.
proposals.reason: 若羅拔能等 is Ruluobaneng and others, not a collective confederation-name in place of the man.

proposals.after: Lady Yang (羊氏), dowager empress of the Hongxun palace, passed away.

proposals.before: Empress Yang of the Hongxun palace died.
proposals.after: Empress Yang (羊氏) of the Hongxun palace died.
proposals.reason: 羊氏 is the Yang clan written 羊, not 楊.

proposals.after: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jichou, Empress Jingxian, lady Yang (羊氏), was given joint burial at Junping mausoleum.
proposals.reason: 羊氏 is the Yang clan written 羊, not 楊.

proposals.after: In the ninth month: He Zeng rose from grand tutor to grand preceptor.

proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 程據 (Cheng Ju).

proposals.before: Dingwei: He Zeng, grand preceptor, died.
proposals.after: Dingwei: He Zeng, grand preceptor and duke of Langling, died.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the ducal title Langling (朗陵公).

proposals.before: November: the conquest of Wu opened on every vector—Sima Zhou from Tu, Wang Hun from the north bank, Wang Rong, Hu Fen, Du Yu, and a river fleet under Wang Jun and Tang Bin—over two hundred thousand soldiers [24].
proposals.after: In the eleventh month: the conquest of Wu opened on every vector—Sima Zhou from Tu, Wang Hun from the north bank, Wang Rong, Hu Fen, Du Yu, and a river fleet under Wang Jun and Tang Bin—over two hundred thousand soldiers [24].
proposals.reason: 十一月 is the lunar eleventh month, not November.

proposals.before: December: Ma Long killed Shujineng and recovered Liangzhou.
proposals.after: In the twelfth month: Ma Long killed Shujineng and recovered Liangzhou.
proposals.reason: 十二月 is the lunar twelfth month, not December.

proposals.before: Gengshen: Xiling fell; Liu Xian, Cheng Quan, and Zheng Guang died defending it [25].
proposals.after: Gengshen: Xiling fell; Liu Xian, Cheng Qu, and Zheng Guang died defending it [25].
proposals.reason: 成璩 is Cheng Qu. Quan misreads 璩.

proposals.before: On the day gengshen they also took Xiling, killing Xiling commander and general who guards the army Liu Xian [25], general who campaigns south Cheng Quan, and Xiling intendant Zheng Guang.
proposals.after: On the day gengshen they also took Xiling, killing Xiling commander and general who guards the army Liu Xian [25], general who campaigns south Cheng Qu, and Xiling intendant Zheng Guang.
proposals.reason: 成璩 is Cheng Qu. Quan misreads 璩.

proposals.before: At Banqiao Wang Hun and Zhou Jun killed Zhang Ti and his lieutenants and shipped the heads north.
proposals.after: At Banqiao Wang Hun and Zhou Jun killed Zhang Ti and his generals Sun Zhen (孫震) and Shen Ying (沈瑩) and shipped the heads north.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 孫震 and 沈瑩, who were beheaded with Zhang Ti.

proposals.before: Envoys fanned out through the new south to reassure the conquered.
proposals.after: Zhang Ce, acting palace attendant, and Zhu Zhen, gentleman of the yellow gate, were sent through Yang and Yue to reassure the newly submitted.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 張側 and 朱震.

proposals.before: Xinhai: Sun Hao became “return-the-mandate” marquis while his sons received court sinecures.
proposals.after: Xinhai of the fifth month: Sun Hao was enfeoffed as marquis who returns the mandate; his crown prince was appointed gentleman of the interior, and his other sons gentlemen.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the fifth month, the crown prince's appointment as 中郎, and the other sons' appointment as 郎中.

proposals.before: Fallen Wu generals’ families were resettled at Shouyang; southern officials got ten years’ tax holiday, commoners twenty.
proposals.after: Families of Sun generals who had died in battle were moved to Shouyang; officers and clerks who had crossed the Yangzi had labor remitted for ten years, commoners and artisans for twenty.
proposals.reason: 孫氏大將戰亡之家 are families of Sun generals killed in battle. 將吏渡江 are officers who crossed the river, and the remission is of labor service (復), not a tax holiday.

proposals.before: Bingyin [29]: Sun Hao was paraded before the court amid cheers.
proposals.after: Bingyin [29]: the emperor came to the hall for a great assembly, led Sun Hao up into the hall, and the ministers all cried 'ten thousand years.'
proposals.reason: 引皓升殿 is leading Sun Hao up into the hall, not parading him.

proposals.before: Dingmao: Luling wine was poured for the ancestors.
proposals.after: Dingmao: Linglu wine was poured for the ancestors.
proposals.reason: 酃淥酒 is Linglu wine, not wine from Luling (廬陵).

proposals.before: On the day dingmao fine wine from Luling was offered in the grand temple.
proposals.after: On the day dingmao fine wine from Linglu was offered in the grand temple.
proposals.reason: 酃淥酒 is Linglu wine, not wine from Luling (廬陵).

proposals.before: Gengchen: Wang Jun, Du Yu, Wang Rong, and Tang Bin received marquisates while Jia Chong and Sima Zhou gained added revenue.
proposals.after: Gengchen: Wang Jun was made great general who assists the state and marquis of Xiangyang, Du Yu marquis of Dangyang, Wang Rong marquis of Anfeng, Tang Bin marquis of Shangyong, and Jia Chong, Sima Zhou the king of Langye, and those below them received increased fiefs.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the offices and the marquisate names, and calls 增封 added revenue.

proposals.before: Sima Mu regained kingship as ruler of Gaoyang.
proposals.after: Sima Mu, marquis of Danshui, was enfeoffed as king of Gaoyang.
proposals.reason: The text is 封丹水侯睦爲高陽王. It does not say he regained a kingdom.

proposals.before: Seventh month: steppe raider Kecheni hit Xiping and Gaomen, killing three hundred officers.
proposals.after: Seventh month: steppe raider Kecheni hit Xiping and Haomen, killing three hundred officers.
proposals.reason: 浩亹 is Haomen, not Gaomen.

proposals.before: In autumn, the seventh month, the tribesman Kecheni raided Xiping and Gaomen, killing more than three hundred commanders and captains downward.
proposals.after: In autumn, the seventh month, the tribesman Kecheni raided Xiping and Haomen, killing more than three hundred commanders and captains downward.
proposals.reason: 浩亹 is Haomen, not Gaomen.

proposals.before: Cheshi’s forward king sent his heir to Luoyang.
proposals.after: In the eighth month the forward division of Cheshi sent a son to serve at court.
proposals.reason: 車師前部遣子入侍 names the forward division, not a king, and does not say Luoyang. 子 is a son sent to serve, not necessarily an heir.

proposals.before: Jiwei: Prince Yanzuo became king of Leping.
proposals.after: Jiwei: the imperial younger brother Yanzuo was enfeoffed as king of Leping.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 皇弟 (imperial younger brother).

proposals.before: Wuchen: Sima Zan of Guanghan died.
proposals.after: Twelfth month, wuchen: Sima Zan, king of Guanghan, died.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 十二月.

proposals.before: Taikang 2, spring: Huainan and Danyang shook.
proposals.after: Taikang 2, spring, second month: Huainan and Danyang suffered earthquakes.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 二月.

proposals.before: Summer: five more Yi peoples asked for enrollment.
proposals.after: Summer, sixth month: five states of the eastern Yi submitted.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 六月, and 內附 is submission, not a request.

proposals.before: Floods on the Yangzi and at Taishan displaced three hundred families.
proposals.after: Floods at Jiangxia and Mount Tai swept away more than three hundred households.
proposals.reason: 江夏 is Jiangxia, not the Yangzi. 三百餘家 is more than three hundred households.

proposals.before: August: a comet crossed the Zhang mansion.
proposals.after: Eighth month: a broom star appeared in the Zhang lunar lodge.
proposals.reason: 八月 is the lunar eighth month, not August. 張 is the Zhang lodge, and 星孛 is a broom star.

proposals.before: Winter: Xianbei chief Murong Hui struck Changli.
proposals.after: Winter, tenth month: Murong Hui of the Xianbei raided Changli.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 十月.

proposals.before: Jiawu: Zhang Hua took command on the Youzhou frontier.
proposals.after: Jiawu: Zhang Hua, a master of writing, was appointed commander of all military affairs in You province.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 尚書 and the exact office 都督幽州諸軍事.

proposals.before: Intercalary bingzi: Li Yin, steward of the masters of the people, died.
proposals.after: Intercalary bingzi: Li Yin, Minister over the Masses, died.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister over the Masses. The idiomatic English also drops the marquisate of Guanglu, which the literal keeps.

proposals.before: In the intercalary month, on the day bingzi, Li Yin, steward of the masters of the people and marquis of Guanglu, died.
proposals.after: In the intercalary month, on the day bingzi, Li Yin, minister over the masses and marquis of Guanglu, died.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is minister over the masses, not a literal 'steward of the masters of the people'.

proposals.before: Seventh month [31]: Pingzhou was struck from the map, and Ning’s governor no longer had to make the old triennial appearance in Luoyang.
proposals.after: Seventh month [31]: the requirement that the inspectors of Ping province and Ning province come to court to report once every three years was abolished.
proposals.reason: 罷平州、寧州刺史三年一入奏事 abolishes the triennial court report of both inspectors. It does not abolish Ping province.

proposals.before: In autumn, the seventh month [31], Ping province was abolished, and the practice whereby the inspector of Ning province journeyed to court once every three years to present memorials was abolished.
proposals.after: In autumn, the seventh month [31], The requirement that the inspectors of Ping province and Ning province come to court to report once every three years was abolished.
proposals.reason: The literal English wrongly abolishes Ping province and limits the triennial report to Ning.

proposals.before: Two ex-Wu officers, Wan Gong and Bo Feng, murdered the Jianye magistrate and besieged Yangzhou until Xu inspector Ji Xi crushed the rising.
proposals.after: Two ex-Wu officers, Guan Gong and Bo Feng, murdered the Jianye magistrate and besieged Yangzhou until Xu inspector Ji Xi crushed the rising.
proposals.reason: 莞 as a surname is read Guan. Wan misreads 莞.

proposals.before: Former Wu generals Wan Gong and Bo Feng raised troops in revolt, killed the magistrate of Jianye, then besieged Yang province; Ji Xi, inspector of Xu province, campaigned and pacified them.
proposals.after: Former Wu generals Guan Gong and Bo Feng raised troops in revolt, killed the magistrate of Jianye, then besieged Yang province; Ji Xi, inspector of Xu province, campaigned and pacified them.
proposals.reason: 莞 as a surname is read Guan. Wan misreads 莞.

proposals.before: Winter, twelfth month, jiashen: Sima You, King of Qi and Minister of Works, was made Grand Marshal and supervisor of all military affairs in Qing province; Sima Zhou, Great General Who Garrisons the East and King of Langye, was made Great General Who Pacifies the Army; [32] Sima Liang, King of Runan, was made Grand Commandant; Shan Tao, Grand Master of Brilliant Prosperity, was made Minister over the Masses; and Wei Guan, Director of the Secretariat, was made Minister of Works.
proposals.after: Winter, twelfth month, jiashen: Sima You, King of Qi and Minister of Works, was made Grand Marshal and supervisor of all military affairs in Qing province; Sima Zhou, Great General Who Garrisons the East and King of Langye, was made Great General Who Pacifies the Army; [32] Sima Liang, King of Runan, was made Grand Commandant; Shan Tao, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, was made Minister over the Masses; and Wei Guan, Director of the Secretariat, was made Minister of Works.
proposals.reason: 光祿大夫 is Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, not Brilliant Prosperity.

proposals.before: On the day jiashen of winter, twelfth month, Sima You, king of Qi and minister of works, was made grand marshal and supervisor of all military affairs of Qing province; Sima Zhou, great general who guards the east and king of Langye, was made great general who pacifies the army [32]; Sima Liang, king of Runan, grand commandant; Shan Tao, grand officer of brilliant prosperity, steward of the masters of the people; Wei Guan, supervisor of the masters of writing, minister of works.
proposals.after: On the day jiashen of winter, twelfth month, Sima You, king of Qi and minister of works, was made grand marshal and supervisor of all military affairs of Qing province; Sima Zhou, great general who guards the east and king of Langye, was made great general who pacifies the army [32]; Sima Liang, king of Runan, grand commandant; Shan Tao, grand master for splendid happiness, steward of the masters of the people; Wei Guan, supervisor of the masters of writing, minister of works.
proposals.reason: 光祿大夫 is grand master for splendid happiness, not brilliant prosperity.

proposals.before: Taikang 4, jiashen [33]: Wei Shu and Sima Huang took the left and right vice-presidencies.
proposals.after: Taikang 4, spring, first month, jiashen [33]: Wei Shu moved from right vice-president of the secretariat to left vice-president, and Sima Huang, king of Xiapi, became right vice-president.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 春正月 and the kingship of Xiapi, and it collapses two different appointments.

proposals.before: Jichou: Shi was promoted from Changle village marquis to king of Beihai.
proposals.after: Jichou of the second month: Shi, marquis of Changle village, was established as king of Beihai.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 二月. 立 is established, not necessarily promoted.

proposals.before: Summer: Sima Ling of Rencheng died.
proposals.after: Summer, fourth month: Sima Ling, king of Rencheng, died.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 四月.

proposals.before: Jihai: Sima Zhou, king of Langye, died.
proposals.after: Jihai of the fifth month: Sima Zhou, great general and king of Langye, died.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 五月 and the office 大將軍.

proposals.before: The Liaodong princedom was downgraded to Donglai for Sima Rui.
proposals.after: Sima Rui was transferred from king of Liaodong to king of Donglai.
proposals.reason: 徙 is a transfer of fief. The text does not say the princedom was downgraded.

proposals.before: June: salaries for the nine chamberlains were raised.
proposals.after: Sixth month: the ritual stipends of the nine ministers were increased.
proposals.reason: 六月 is the lunar sixth month. 禮秩 is ritual rank and stipend, not only salary.

proposals.before: Renzi: Sima Huang took Qing military command.
proposals.after: Renzi of the seventh month: Sima Huang, king of Xiapi and right vice-president, was made commander of all military affairs in Qing province.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 七月, 下邳王, and 尚書右僕射.

proposals.before: Shanshan sent a royal hostage and received the “return to righteousness” marquis title.
proposals.after: Eighth month: Shanshan sent a son to serve at court, and he was provisionally made marquis who returns to righteousness.
proposals.reason: The title 歸義侯 is given to the son (假其), and the English drops 八月.

proposals.before: Wuwu: Sima Gai of Xindu died.
proposals.after: Wuwu of the eleventh month: Sima Gai, king of Xindu, died.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 十一月.

proposals.before: Wei Shu became steward of the masters of the people.
proposals.after: Wei Shu became minister over the masses.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is minister over the masses.

proposals.before: Wei Shu of the masters of writing was appointed steward of the masters of the people.
proposals.after: Wei Shu of the masters of writing was appointed minister over the masses.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is minister over the masses.

proposals.before: Gengwu: another parade at Xuanwu.
proposals.after: Gengwu of the twelfth month: a grand review was held at the Xuanwu stand.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 十二月 and adds 'another', which is not in the text.

proposals.before: Bingwu: a roof-beam snapped in Gaozu’s temple.
proposals.after: Bingwu: a roof-beam snapped in Emperor Xuan's temple.
proposals.reason: 宣帝 is Emperor Xuan of Jin, not Gaozu.

proposals.before: Bingyin: Prince Dian of the southern palace became king of Changle.
proposals.after: Bingyin of the second month: Dian, son of the king of the Southern Palace, was established as king of Changle.
proposals.reason: 南宮王子 means son of the king of the Southern Palace. The English drops 二月 and the kinship.

proposals.before: June: the “Yellow Sand” review prison was created.
proposals.after: Sixth month: the “Yellow Sand” review prison was created.
proposals.reason: 六月 is the lunar sixth month, not June.

proposals.before: Seventh month, wushen: Prince Hui died.
proposals.after: Seventh month, wushen: the imperial son Hui died.
proposals.reason: 皇子 is an imperial son. 'Prince Hui' drops that.

proposals.before: September brought gales, floods in five provinces, and black frost.
proposals.after: The ninth month brought gales, floods in five provinces, and black frost.
proposals.reason: 九月 is the lunar ninth month, not September.

proposals.before: Jiachen: Sima Fu of Taiyuan died.
proposals.after: Jiachen of the eleventh month: Sima Fu (輔), king of Taiyuan, died.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 十一月. 輔 is not 孚.

proposals.before: Gengwu: general amnesty.
proposals.after: Gengwu of the twelfth month: a great amnesty.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 十二月.

proposals.before: Intercalary month: Du Yu died.
proposals.after: Intercalary month: Du Yu, great general who guards the south and marquis of Dangyang, died.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 鎮南大將軍 and 當陽侯.

proposals.before: March frost hurt mulberries and wheat in six jurisdictions.
proposals.after: The third month frost hurt mulberries and wheat in six jurisdictions.
proposals.reason: 三月 is the lunar third month, not March.

proposals.before: Bingzi: Liu Kang, last Han-title noble, died.
proposals.after: Bingzi of the ninth month: Liu Kang, duke of Shanyang, died.
proposals.reason: The text says 山陽公. 'Last Han-title noble' is a gloss, and 九月 is dropped.

proposals.before: Winter: landslides and flash floods in Nan’an.
proposals.after: Winter, tenth month: landslides and flash floods in Nan’an.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 十月.

proposals.before: Jiashen: a ten-day army review at Xuanwu.
proposals.after: Jiashen of the twelfth month: a grand review at the Xuanwu stand lasted ten days.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 十二月.

proposals.before: Summer drought gripped thirteen provinces.
proposals.after: Summer, fifth month: thirteen commanderies and principalities had drought.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 五月 and turns 郡國 into provinces.

proposals.before: Murong Hui struck Liaodong again.
proposals.after: Murong Hui of the Xianbei raided Liaodong.
proposals.reason: The text does not say the raid was a repeat. 鮮卑 is dropped.

proposals.before: August: eleven Yi peoples asked to join Jin.
proposals.after: Eighth month: eleven Yi peoples asked to join Jin.
proposals.reason: 八月 is the lunar eighth month, not August.

proposals.before: Wuyin: Sima Jun of Fufeng died.
proposals.after: Wuyin of the ninth month: Sima Jun, general of the agile cavalry and king of Fufeng, died.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 九月 and 驃騎將軍.

proposals.before: Censors toured flood-hit counties with relief mandates.
proposals.after: Twelfth month: investigating censors were sent to tour commanderies that had suffered flood.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 十二月 and adds relief mandates the text does not state. 郡 are commanderies.

proposals.before: Two hundred seventy palace women of lower rank were freed to marry out.
proposals.after: Two hundred seventy palace women of lower rank were sent home.
proposals.reason: 歸于家 is sent home. The text does not say they were freed to marry.

proposals.before: Taikang 5, jihai: two blue dragons in the Luoyang arsenal well.
proposals.after: Taikang 5, jihai: two azure dragons in the Luoyang arsenal well.
proposals.reason: 青龍 are azure dragons. Literal already says azure.

proposals.before: September: plans to rebuild the ancestral temple.
proposals.after: Ninth month: plans to rebuild the ancestral temple.
proposals.reason: 九月 is the lunar ninth month, not September.

proposals.before: Winter: Li Feng’s mutiny in southern Jiangxi.
proposals.after: Winter, tenth month: Li Feng, a clerk of Pinggu county in Nankang, rebelled, gathered a crowd, attacked the commanderies and counties, and styled himself general.
proposals.reason: 南康 is Nankang, not southern Jiangxi. The idiomatic English drops the month, the office, and the rebellion.

proposals.before: November: Xiao Fu rose at Hai’an.
proposals.after: Eleventh month: Xiao Fu rose at Hai’an.
proposals.reason: 十一月 is the lunar eleventh month, not November.

proposals.before: December: Jiang Di’s band in Wu-xing was wiped out.
proposals.after: Twelfth month: Jiang Di’s band in Wu-xing was wiped out.
proposals.reason: 十二月 is the lunar twelfth month, not December.

proposals.before: The lower Yangzi region shook in four counties.
proposals.after: The four commanderies east of the Yangzi suffered an earthquake.
proposals.reason: 江東四郡 is four commanderies east of the Yangzi, not four counties of the lower Yangzi.

proposals.before: February: Hu Fen died; Zhu Zheng took his secretariat seat.
proposals.after: Second month: Hu Fen, right vice-president and marquis of Yangxia, died; Zhu Zheng, a master of writing, was made right vice-president.
proposals.reason: 二月 is the lunar second month. The idiomatic English drops both titles.

proposals.before: May: Sima Qi of Yiyang lost his kingship for crime, becoming village marquis of Sanzongting.
proposals.after: Fifth month: Sima Qi of Yiyang lost his kingship for crime, becoming village marquis of Sanzongting.
proposals.reason: 五月 is the lunar fifth month, not May.

proposals.before: Taikang 10, summer: Liu Xiao and Liang Liu each won a thousand-hu bounty for good rule.
proposals.after: Taikang 10, summer, fourth month: Liu Xiao, prefect of Jingzhao, and Liang Liu, prefect of Yangping, were each granted a thousand hu of grain for their administration.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 四月 and the two prefectures.

proposals.before: May: Murong Hui yielded while eleven Yi realms joined Jin.
proposals.after: Fifth month: Murong Hui yielded while eleven Yi realms joined Jin.
proposals.reason: 五月 is the lunar fifth month, not May.

proposals.before: Gengzi: Liu Jin, mountain-yang duke, died.
proposals.after: Gengzi of the sixth month: Liu Jin, duke of Shanyang, died.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 六月. 山陽公 is duke of Shanyang.

proposals.before: On the day bingchen of the eleventh month Xun Xu, acting supervisor of the masters of writing and grand officer of the left brilliance, died.
proposals.after: On the day bingchen of the eleventh month Xun Xu, acting supervisor of the masters of writing and grand master for splendid happiness on the left, died.
proposals.reason: 左光祿大夫 is grand master for splendid happiness on the left, not brilliance.

proposals.before: On the day jiazi of the third month Shi Jian, grand officer of the right brilliance, was appointed minister of works.
proposals.after: On the day jiazi of the third month Shi Jian, grand master for splendid happiness on the right, was appointed minister of works.
proposals.reason: 右光祿大夫 is grand master for splendid happiness on the right.

proposals.before: Jiyou: the emperor expired in Hanzhang at fifty-five, resting as Shizu at Junyang.
proposals.after: Jiyou: the emperor expired in Hanzhang at fifty-five, buried at the Junyang tomb with the temple name Shizu.
proposals.reason: 葬峻陽陵，廟號世祖 is burial at Junyang with temple name Shizu, not 'resting as'.

proposals.before: For Prince Dian of Nangong becoming King of Changle, the biography of King Xian of Anping, Fu, writes "You" for "Dian," and Taiping Huanyu Ji 63 also writes "You."
proposals.after: For Dian, son of the Prince of Nangong, becoming King of Changle, the biography of King Xian of Anping, Fu, writes "You" for "Dian," and Taiping Huanyu Ji 63 also writes "You."
proposals.reason: 南宮王子玷 is Dian, son of the Prince of Nangong, not Prince Dian of Nangong.

proposals.before: Regarding “Prince Dian of the southern palace as king of Changle”: the biography of Prince Xian of Anping writes the name You, and Taiping huanyu ji 63 also writes You.
proposals.after: Regarding “Dian, son of the Prince of Nangong, as king of Changle”: the biography of King Xian of Anping, Fu writes the name You, and Taiping huanyu ji 63 also writes You.
proposals.reason: 南宮 is the fief Nangong, not the southern palace, and 子玷 is the prince's son. 安平獻王孚 is King Xian of Anping, Fu.

proposals.before: Regarding establishing Ying, son of Hejian’s peaceful king Hong, as king of Zhangwu: the biography of Hejian king Hong lists only two sons, Wei and Hun, and none named Ying.
proposals.after: Regarding establishing Ying, son of King Ping of Hejian Hong, as king of Zhangwu: the biography of Hejian king Hong lists only two sons, Wei and Hun, and none named Ying.
proposals.reason: 河間平王 is King Ping of Hejian. 平 is the posthumous title, not the adjective peaceful.

proposals.before: Succession shifts to Hun after Wei’s transfer.
proposals.after: Later Wei went out to succeed Wang, Prince of Yiyang, and Hun was established as heir.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops 義陽王望, the prince Wei went out to succeed.

proposals.before: Under the sixth year of Xianhe in the Chengji annals, there is the text, “Zhen, son of Hun, King Wu of Zhangwu, was made King of Zhangwu”; therefore the “Ying” here should be an error for the graph “Hun.”
proposals.after: Under the sixth year of Xianhe in the Chengji annals, there is the text, “Zhen, son of Hun, King of Zhangwu, was made King of Zhangwu”; therefore the “Ying” here should be an error for the graph “Hun.”
proposals.reason: 章武 is the fief Zhangwu. 章武王 is king of Zhangwu, not King Wu of Zhangwu.

proposals.before: Regarding “one hundred thousand persons of the Xihe tribe came to surrender”: editions all insert the two characters renxu above Xihe.
proposals.after: Regarding “one hundred thousand persons of the Xike tribe came to surrender”: editions all insert the two characters renxu above Xike.
proposals.reason: 奚軻 is Xike, as the idiomatic English has it. Xihe is a different name.

decisions.reason: 新昌鄉侯 is the marquisate of Xinchang township; Xinxiang would require 新鄉.
新昌鄉侯 is Xinchang, not Xinxiang.
中撫軍 is Sima Yan’s office (central commander of the army), not a force named the Central Pacification Army.
縣人王始 is one county man, Wang Shi, not “the people of the district” plus an appositive.
